::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 25th [1867]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 174-175
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
The <u>[Chaplet of Pearls](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd)</u> is done, and I shall send it by train tomorrow, being glad to get it out of the house, as it entices me into touching it up when I ought to be doing other things. I am afraid you will think that though it is not a story without an end, yet the end is very far away - but it <u>would</u> not be shorter, and judging by the number of chapters I do not think it is as long as [Redclyffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd). I do not think it would shorten without taking away the sense of time and proportion - which is wanted in a finished tale, though not so much in a magazine. I have had editorship enough to know what an unfinished story is. I made a resolution at first about accepting any tale without its end, and never broke it without being sorry for it - even with people I could trust.

I saw [Miss Wilbraham](people/person_1513.qmd) on Saturday and I think she seems likely to be able to write for the [Sunday Library](organizations/other_145.qmd) - but her [mother](people/person_1982.qmd) is such an invalid that she is always rather uncertain.

I must write about the Penny Readings when I have thought more about them.

I must put a note to the Chaplet begging people not to think it a controversial tale - is it any use to do this to the 1st chapter in the [Magazine](organizations/other_78.qmd), or had it better wait to be a preface to the whole?

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge
